the-iron-claw-2023.gazette: The Von Erichs promoted wrestling out of Dallas, and their run through the 1980s sits in the public record — territory footage, newspaper obituaries, a father's own booking sheets. Durkin's film leaves one brother out of the family altogether, on the reasoning that the real sequence of deaths would play as implausible on screen. The omission is the most visible edit made to a history that is otherwise fully documented.

the-promised-land-2023.gazette: The Danish crown spent the middle of the eighteenth century trying to make the Jutland heath pay, offering land, settlers and a title to anyone who could raise a crop on ground nobody wanted. Ludvig Kahlen was a real captain who took that offer, and the German colonists he recruited belong to the same record. The film's central bargain — cultivate the moor, receive a noble patent — is the actual wording of the deal.

the-zone-of-interest-2023.gazette: Rudolf Höss ran Auschwitz from a house on the other side of the wall, where his wife kept a garden against it and the children were raised within earshot. He set his own account down on paper in Polish custody after the war and was hanged in 1947 a short walk from that garden. Glazer built the household from the surviving record of the site and kept the camp itself off screen, entirely in sound.
the-zone-of-interest-2023.prism: Keeping the camp out of frame puts the whole weight on the sound mix, so the atrocity is only ever as present as the audience is willing to hear. The family's ordinariness isn't a discovery either — it's what the paperwork already said.

totem-2023.gazette: The whole film takes place inside one house across a single day, the camera moving room to room among relatives assembling a birthday party for a father dying in the back bedroom. Avilés keeps the frame crowded and unremarkable — a kitchen at work, a locked bathroom door, an aunt smoking — and lets the seven-year-old at the center find her own way through it. Nothing is explained to her, and nothing is explained on her behalf.

a-complete-unknown-2024.gazette: Newport, July 1965: Dylan came on with an electric band and a short set, and what the crowd actually did that afternoon has been argued over ever since, with the recordings and the eyewitnesses refusing to agree. Mangold works from a career documented down to the setlists, and had the performances sung live rather than dubbed to playback. Even the story about Pete Seeger and an axe survives mainly as a story.

all-we-imagine-as-light-2024.gazette: Kapadia opens on Mumbai at night in the voices of people who came there for work, unseen, describing the years the city takes before it returns anything. The two nurses at the center are Malayali migrants, part of a labor route out of Kerala into Indian hospitals that has been running for generations, and the film keeps their shifts, their shared rent and their commutes in view. She made documentaries before this, and the city is shot that way.
all-we-imagine-as-light-2024.prism: Once a film has shown you how the rent and the shift roster actually work, the trip to the coast can only be a break in the schedule, not an exit from it. Kapadia films it as the break, and lets the city keep waiting.

black-dog-2024.gazette: Ahead of the 2008 Games, towns across China cleared their strays and emptied their condemned blocks on a timetable set in Beijing, thousands of miles from where anything would be held. Guan Hu puts the film in one of those towns on the edge of the Gobi, with a patrol rounding up dogs and a demolition crew working the same streets. The Olympics arrive there only as a countdown on someone else's television.

conclave-2024.gazette: The Vatican does not lend its interiors, so the Sistine Chapel, the Casa Santa Marta and the corridors between them were rebuilt at Cinecittà and lit as though the cardinals had nowhere else to be. The procedure is public and the film follows it: the doors closed on extra omnes, the sequestered lodgings, the ballots counted and burned, the two-thirds threshold, smoke as the only signal permitted to leave the room. Viewers checked the rite line by line, which is the nearest thing a thriller gets to a fact-check.

dahomey-2024.gazette: France returned twenty-six works to Benin in November 2021, crated out of the Quai Branly more than a century after they were taken from Abomey. Diop films the packing, the flight, the unpacking and the state ceremony, then gives most of the running time to students at the University of Abomey-Calavi arguing over what twenty-six objects settle. The debate is real, held on campus, and it does not resolve.
dahomey-2024.prism: Twenty-six back and thousands still in French storerooms makes the ceremony an accounting statement as much as a homecoming, and the students read it that way. The odd move is letting a statue narrate: the only party with standing to speak is the one that cannot be cross-examined.

i-m-still-here-2024.gazette: Rubens Paiva, a former congressman, was taken from his house in Rio in 1971 and never came back; the army denied holding him, and the family spent decades with no document to show. Brazil issued his death certificate in 2014, after a truth commission finally put the disappearance in writing. Salles knew that household as a teenager, and the film gives most of its length to the years in between, when nothing was confirmed and the family kept going.

maria-2024.gazette: Callas spent her last years in an apartment on the avenue Georges-Mandel and died there in September 1977, at fifty-three, long after the voice had left the stage. Larraín takes that final stretch in Paris and runs the documented life back through it — the Onassis years, the cancelled performances, the recordings that outlasted the instrument. Jolie trained for months to sing, and what reaches the soundtrack is her voice mixed under Callas's own.

on-becoming-a-guinea-fowl-2024.gazette: A woman driving home at night finds her uncle's body in the road, and the days that follow keep her inside a mourning house run by aunts who know exactly how a funeral goes. Nyoni plays the rites straight — the wailing on cue, the seating order, the cooking and the grieving both done on schedule — and lets what nobody says sit in the room with everyone. The abuse was common knowledge inside the family long before it was spoken in front of it.
on-becoming-a-guinea-fowl-2024.prism: The ritual works, which is the problem: it hands everybody something correct to do for a week, and by the end the man is buried properly and the girls have still not been asked anything. Silence here isn't a failure of the family — it's one of the services the family provides.

santosh-2024.gazette: Indian states let a government post pass to the widow under compassionate appointment, and that is how Santosh ends up in a constable's uniform in a small northern town. Suri came out of documentary, shoots the station at eye level, and stays in the room for the interrogation rather than cutting to the corridor. The caste of the missing girl determines how the case gets worked, and the film treats that as procedure rather than revelation.

sing-sing-2024.gazette: Rehabilitation Through the Arts has been staging theater inside Sing Sing since 1996, and the play at the center of this film — a time-travel comedy the group really performed — came out of that program. Most of the cast are RTA alumni playing versions of themselves opposite Colman Domingo, Clarence Maclin among them, working through his own history on camera. The production paid everyone the same rate and split the back end evenly, a term reported almost as widely as the performances.

sujo-2024.gazette: A cartel gunman is killed in the opening minutes, and the film stays with what he left behind: a small boy, an aunt, a house at the end of a dirt road in Michoacán. Valadez and Rondero hold the camera still and keep the violence at the edge of the frame, where it works less as event than as weather. Sujo grows up somewhere the work available to him is known in advance, and the film spends its length on the years before he has to answer for it.
sujo-2024.prism: Refusing the shootouts means refusing the payment the genre usually makes to its audience, and what's left is arithmetic — who gets offered a way out, who gets offered one job. A boy who reaches a classroom in the capital isn't proof the road exists; he's one route out of a place where most of the frame stays put.
